title: Printer Rate Became Per Printer Per Minute
text: id: COMP-005 domain: math title: Printer Rate Became Per Printer Per Minute tags: rates, printers, unit-rate memory: A printer problem became clear only when I found the per-printer-per-minute rate. Four printers and six minutes made a combined work window, not a single machine. I divided pages by printers and minutes, then rebuilt the new combined rate for the smaller printer group. I wrote the combined rate explicitly as printers times per-printer rate, with pages per minute beside it, before dividing pages by that rate. The final time carried minutes, not pages.

title: The Two Minute Printer Answer Was A Denominator Failure
text: id: COMP-027 domain: math title: The Two Minute Printer Answer Was A Denominator Failure tags: printer, rate, negative-outcome, correction memory: I once answered 2 minutes on a printer-rate problem because I treated 480 divided by 4 as 120 pages per minute. That was wrong; it was 120 pages per printer over 6 minutes. The corrected rate was 120 divided by 6, or 20 pages per printer per minute. Three printers then made 60 pages per minute, and 720 pages divided by 60 pages per minute gave 12 minutes.

title: Printer Minutes Stayed In The Denominator
text: id: COMP-021 domain: math title: Printer Minutes Stayed In The Denominator tags: printers, rates, denominator, correction memory: I once divided pages by printers and accidentally called the result pages per minute. The missed denominator was time. The correction was pages divided by printers divided by minutes: 480 pages divided by 4 printers divided by 6 minutes gave 20 pages per printer per minute. Only after that did 3 printers become a 60 pages per minute combined rate. The visible line I wrote was: 3 printers times 20 pages per minute equals 60 pages per minute. That mistake made me keep minutes in the denominator until the unit said pages per minute.
